tool.name: Growler LASTZ
tool.description: : gapped extension of one chromosome pair
tool.command:
## Growler maps this tool over a collection of pair files. One pair file = every anchor segment for one ## (target, query) chromosome pair, both strands. One job, one lastz, one output element, and ## the element identifier is carried through unchanged by Galaxy.
## ⛔ THE 2BITS MUST BE SYMLINKED TO A `.2bit` NAME. lastz decides a sequence file is 2bit from ## its FILENAME, and a Galaxy dataset on disk is `dataset_<uuid>.dat`. Handed the bare dataset ## path, lastz tries to parse it as FASTA and fails on the binary header. The symlink is not ## tidiness; without it the tool cannot work at all. ln -s '$target' target.2bit && ln -s '$query' query.2bit &&
## ⛔ AND THE KEG MUST BE DECOMPRESSED FIRST. Pair files ship gzipped because segments are 97.1% of a ## bundle and compress ~3.6x -- shipping them plain would roughly triple the object store. But ## `--segments=<file>.gz` does not fail loudly: lastz reads the gzip header as text and reports ## `FAILURE: bad field (...: line 1, ...)` while still producing an empty output file. Measured ## 2026-09-17. So decompress here, and only here. ## ## This costs ~140 MB per job. The tarball path it replaces inflated the ENTIRE bundle -- 14.58 GB ## on the pair this was measured against -- into the job directory before running anything. gzip -cdfq '$pair' > pair.segments &&
lastz 'target.2bit[nameparse=darkspace][multiple]' 'query.2bit[nameparse=darkspace]'
## ⚠ 2G pins lastz >= 1.04.41: the value overflows a signed int in earlier builds, which is why ## KegAlign's own copy of the reader uses 1.99G and this one does not. @LASTZ_VERSION@ is 1.04.52. --allocate:traceback=2G --segments=pair.segments
## ⚠ NO `--strand`. A pair file holds both strands, written plus-before-minus as the lastz manual ## requires, and lastz's default is `both`. Passing `--strand=plus` here would silently drop ## every minus-strand segment in the pair file -- measured identical output with the flag omitted. #if $scores --scores='$scores' #end if --format='$format_selector' --gappedthresh=$gappedthresh --ydrop=$ydrop #if str($interpolation.inner_selector) == "yes" --inner=$interpolation.inner #end if --output='$output'

param.name: pair
param.label: Chromosome pair
param.help: One element of a KegAlign pair file collection: the anchor segments for a single chromosome pair, both strands, gzipped.

param.name: scores
param.label: Scoring file in LASTZ format
param.help: Leave unset to use LASTZ's built-in matrix. Must match the scoring KegAlign used for seeding, or the two stages disagree about what a good alignment is.

param.label: Gapped extension threshold
param.help: Must match the value KegAlign generated its commands with.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Growler LASTZ performs the gapped-extension stage for a single **pair file** — one element of the collection KegAlign emits with ``--output-type collection``. A pair file holds every anchor segment for one ``(target, query)`` chromosome pair, both strands, gzipped.
Galaxy maps this tool over the pair file collection, so the chromosome-pair key created by KegAlign is carried all the way through to chaining without a tarball, a command manifest, or a collapse step.
.. class:: infomark
Every job runs the **same** command line; only the pair file differs. There is nothing per-element to route, and no element identifier has to reach a parameter.
**Inputs that must agree with the KegAlign run**
The scoring file, ``--gappedthresh``, ``--ydrop`` and ``--inner`` are the values KegAlign used when it generated its commands. Supplying different ones here is legal and will run, but the two stages will then disagree about what counts as a good alignment.
